frequency_question: How often do structural friction points (subnational vetoes, bureaucratic turf wars, federal-state divides, and domestic political opposition) successfully prevent the signing of a water-sharing treaty renewal prior to deadline?
membership_rule: Includes formal bilateral river or transboundary water treaties requiring renewal or renegotiation between sovereign states sharing an international basin; excludes purely internal water disputes or non-treaty technical memoranda.

cases.name: Indus Waters Treaty implementation and modifications (Permanent Commission context)
Lesotho Highlands Water Project Phase II agreements

coverage_note: 6 major representative transboundary water negotiation cases analyzed; baseline reflects high persistence of treaty renewals despite friction.
known_gaps: Excludes smaller municipal-level cross-border watershed agreements and informal arrangements.
skeleton: Identified bilateral transboundary water renegotiations and renewals globally where structural friction (federal-state friction or intense domestic opposition) was present.
multiplier: 5 hits / 6 total prominent treaty frameworks analyzed where structural friction was actively engaged.
validity_reason: Bilateral hydro-diplomacy norms and institutional structures change slowly over multi-year diplomatic cycles.
